items.title: Identifying Instances of the Vertical Angles Theorem

sections.normalized_html: Consider the above diagrams. In which one can we apply the vertical angles theorem to conclude that the two marked angles are congruent?
sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/7f34e6e42b034ee496fec95a651f1c6d]

Consider the above diagrams. In which one can we apply the vertical angles theorem to conclude that the two marked angles are congruent?

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
The vertical angles theorem says that vertical angles (the opposite angles created by two lines meeting at a point) are congruent.

Let's go through the diagrams:

  • In diagram I, one line and two rays are meeting at a point, rather than two lines.

  • In diagram II, [MATH: \angle 1] and [MATH: \angle 2] are opposite angles created by two lines meeting at a point.

  • In diagram III, [MATH: \angle 1] and [MATH: \angle 2] do not meet at a point, and are alternate interior, not opposite.

So diagram [MATH: \bbox[3pt, gainsboro]{\color{blue}\text{II}}] is the only diagram in which we can apply the vertical angles theorem to [MATH: \angle 1] and [MATH: \angle 2.]

sections.readable_text: Let's recall two important theorems related to alternate interior angles.

    If a transversal cuts two lines and the alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.

    Notice that we added arrows to the diagram on the right.

Let's recall two important theorems related to alternate interior angles.

Content:
- The alternate interior angles theorem states the following:

> If a transversal cuts two parallel lines, then the alternate interior angles are congruent.

In other words, if two lines are parallel, this guarantees that the alternate interior angles are congruent.

[IMG: /graphics/9e209afba78203706aec24bbccad01d4]

Notice that we added angle markers to the diagram on the right.
- The converse alternate interior angles theorem states the following:

> If a transversal cuts two lines and the alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.

Content:

Content:

Item 5 — Tutorial: The Alternate Interior Angle Theorems

Content:
Let's recall two important theorems related to alternate interior angles.

Content:
- The alternate interior angles theorem states the following:

> If a transversal cuts two parallel lines, then the alternate interior angles are congruent.

In other words, if two lines are parallel, this guarantees that the alternate interior angles are congruent.

[IMG: /graphics/9e209afba78203706aec24bbccad01d4]

Notice that we added angle markers to the diagram on the right.
- The converse alternate interior angles theorem states the following:

> If a transversal cuts two lines and the alternate interior angles are congruent, then the lines are parallel.

In other words, if the alternate interior angles are congruent, this guarantees that the lines are parallel.

[IMG: /graphics/b4eb3ba8f11b16e8c409c25925acbbca]

Notice that we added arrows to the diagram on the right.

Content:
Make sure you understand the difference between the two theorems.

Content:
Finally, remember, alternate interior angles are named this way for a reason:

Content:
- Alternate means they lie on opposite sides of the transversal.
- Interior means they lie inside the (parallel) lines.
